docs.title: Stream
docs.text:
Stream is a reactive dataflow esoteric language where the only unit of computation is a gyge — a named node that holds a value, transforms it, or sinks it — and programs are described entirely as flow graphs.

::header::
    <o-> "hello"

::body::
    |greeting| := "Hello, Stream!"
    |greeting| -> |print|

Expected output

Hello, Stream!

docs.title: What makes Stream different
docs.text: Concept Description Single type Everything is a gyge — variable, function, or sink Left-to-right flow \|a\| -> \|b\| -> \|c\| is the core expression form 20 stream operators -> => ~> -!-> -!!-> <~ and 14 more Entropy A runtime value (0–100 Ch) that influences delivery, corruption, and termination Seasons Program-level modifiers (spring, summer, autumn, winter) that shift entropy physics Obfuscation Source can be mechanically transformed into a glyph-dense fucked form at levels 0–9

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • uv (recommended) or pip

docs.title: Clone and install
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/OfekGrunfeld/stream.git
cd stream

# Create a virtual environment and install the package + dev extras
uv venv
uv pip install -e ".[dev]"

The editable install exposes the stream package and the python -m stream CLI entry point.

docs.title: Verify
docs.text:
uv run python -m stream --help

Expected output:

 Usage: python -m stream [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

 Stream language interpreter.

╭─ Commands ──────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ run          Run a Stream source file.               │
│ lex          Tokenise a Stream source file.          │
│ parse        Parse a Stream source file.             │
│ obfuscate    Obfuscate a Stream source file.         │
│ deobfuscate  Deobfuscate a Stream source file.       │
╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

docs.title: Run the test suite
docs.text:
uv run pytest tests/ -q

All tests should pass (187 at the time of writing).

docs.title: Optional: MkDocs preview
docs.text:
uv pip install mkdocs-material
uv run mkdocs serve

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8000.

docs.title: Program structure
docs.text:
Every Stream program is divided into named sections using the ::name:: sigil.

::header::
    <o-> "my_program"
    $S := spring

::body::
    |x| := 42
    |x| -> |print|

Two sections are recognised by the runtime:

Section Purpose ::header:: Metadata and modifiers (name, season, initial entropy) ::body:: Graph topology — gyge declarations and stream edges

docs.title: Gyges
docs.text:
A gyge is the single unit of computation in Stream. Its shape is resolved lazily on first activation:

Shape Description Example VARIABLE Stores and forwards a scalar value \|x\| := 42 FUNCTION Transforms input, emits output \|str\| (built-in) BYTES Raw byte buffer \|buf\| := b"..." PROGRAM Reference to a running process \|self\| := <o> VOID Explicit sink; discards all input \|sink\| := ...

Gyge syntax: |name| — the name is surrounded by pipe characters.

docs.title: Hint prefixes
docs.text:
A hint character after the opening | signals an intended shape to the type registry:

Prefix Hint % function @ program/process target ~ lossy ? conditional ! error path # batch 
|%transform| := ...   <-- hinted as function

docs.title: Stream edges
docs.text:
Stream edges are the arrows between gyges. The full catalogue is in the operators reference; a summary of the most common:

|a| -> |b|        <-- basic: unconditional, entropy-aware delivery
|a| => |b|        <-- priority: delivered before basic edges
|a| ~> |b|        <-- lossy: packets dropped proportionally to entropy
|a| -!-> |b|      <-- error: signals a fault condition
|a| -!!-> |b|     <-- exit: terminates the program
|a| <~ |b|        <-- feedback: back-edge, creates a cycle

docs.title: Entropy
docs.text:
Entropy (Ch, Chaos) is a first-class runtime value ranging from 0 (perfectly ordered) to 100 (full chaos).

  • Starts at entropy_initial (default 15 Ch).
  • Fluctuates every tick based on graph activity.
  • Capped at entropy_cap (default 85 Ch).
  • Raising the cap to 100 enables Terminal Cascade — when entropy hits 100 all buffered packets are corrupted and the program terminates.

Set initial entropy in the header:

::header::
    $entropy := 30

docs.title: Entropy tiers
docs.text: Range Tier Effect 0–20 DORMANT Near-perfect delivery 21–40 CALM Slight jitter 41–60 ACTIVE Occasional packet corruption 61–80 TURBULENT Notable loss on lossy edges 81–99 CRITICAL High corruption, frequent drops 100 CASCADE Terminal Cascade fires (cap must equal 100)

docs.title: Seasons
docs.text:
A season sets the atmospheric modifier that shapes entropy physics.

::header::
    $S := spring    <-- or summer, autumn, winter
Season Entropy bias spring Moderate, stable summer High baseline, volatile autumn Decreasing over time winter Low, cold, predictable

Seasons can be locked ($S := spring) or drift freely (omit $S).

docs.title: Termination
docs.text:
The runtime loop ends for one of four reasons:

Reason Trigger NATURAL_DRAIN All edges empty and no pending output for 3 consecutive ticks EXIT_STREAM A packet reaches a -!!-> edge TERMINAL_CASCADE Entropy reaches 100 while entropy_cap == 100 TICK_LIMIT Safety cap reached (default 100 000 ticks)

docs.title: Comments
docs.text:
<-- This is a comment (single or multiline) -->

<-- Everything between the arrow pairs
    is stripped before lexing. -->

docs.title: The 9-phase tick loop
docs.text:
Every tick executes these phases in order:

Phase Name What it does 0 Entropy Recalculation Compute entropy delta, emit entropy events 1 Modifier Application Apply season / temperature / wind effects 2 Parasite Lifecycle Advance ==> parasite gyges 3 Edge Delivery Move packets from source output ports to destination input ports 4 Node Activation Call fn bodies, store variable values, resolve lazy shapes 5 Entropy Event Resolution Apply queued entropy events (highest impact first) 6 Signal Processing Handle -*-> / -?*-> signal/receive edges 7 Wait Resolution Resolve -,-> wait-stream conditions 8 Graph Mutation Execute queued structural graph changes 9 Garbage Collection Remove drained edges and orphaned nodes

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
All commands are invoked through the stream package:

uv run python -m stream <command> [options] <file>

docs.title: run — Execute a program
docs.text:
uv run python -m stream run examples/01_hello.stream

The HUD is printed every tick showing entropy, node states, and edge buffers. The program terminates with one of four reasons printed in a summary panel.

docs.title: Options
docs.text: Flag Default Description --tick-limit N 100 000 Maximum ticks before forced exit --no-hud — Suppress the Rich HUD (useful for scripting)

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text: Code Meaning 0 Natural drain or exit stream with code 0 1 File not found / parse error 99 Terminal cascade other Value carried by -!!-> packet

docs.title: lex — Inspect tokens
docs.text:
Tokenise a file and print the flat token stream. Useful when debugging lexer behaviour or learning the grammar.

uv run python -m stream lex examples/01_hello.stream

SECTION        'header'     line=13 col=1
ENTRY_POINT    '<o->'       line=14 col=5
STRING         'hello'      line=14 col=10
SECTION        'body'       line=17 col=1
GYGE           'greeting'   line=18 col=5
ASSIGN         ':='         line=18 col=16
STRING         'Hello, ...' line=18 col=19
GYGE           'greeting'   line=19 col=5
STREAM_BASIC   '->'         line=19 col=16
GYGE           'print'      line=19 col=19
EOF                         line=20 col=1

docs.title: parse — Inspect the ASG
docs.text:
Parse a file and print the Abstract Syntax Graph as JSON.

uv run python -m stream parse examples/02_pipeline.stream

The output is the ProgramASG dataclass serialised to a pretty-printed dict, showing all sections, nodes, edges, and header statements.

docs.title: obfuscate — Transform to glyph form
docs.text:
uv run python -m stream obfuscate examples/01_hello.stream --level 3

Writes an obfuscated copy to <stem>.obf.stm by default. Use --output to specify a path.

uv run python -m stream obfuscate examples/01_hello.stream --level 7 --output out.st

Obfuscation levels:

Level What changes 0 Identity — no change 1–2 Operators + delimiters replaced with Unicode glyphs 3–4 Keywords and modifiers also replaced 5–6 Identifiers scrambled (deterministic, seed-based) 7–8 String literals hex-encoded 9 All of the above + whitespace stripped

See the Obfuscator reference for full details.

docs.title: deobfuscate — Restore human-readable form
docs.text:
uv run python -m stream deobfuscate examples/01_hello.st

For levels 1–4 no extra input is needed. For levels 5–9 (scrambled identifiers) pass the symbol table JSON produced during obfuscation:

uv run python -m stream deobfuscate out.st --symbol-table symbols.json

docs.title: Example programs
docs.text:
The examples/ directory contains five annotated programs:

File Demonstrates 01_hello.stream Minimal program — one gyge, one edge 02_pipeline.stream Multi-step chain: \|sentence\| -> \|upper\| -> \|print\| 03_counter.stream Numeric value through \|str\| -> \|print\| 04_lossy.stream ~> lossy edge — probabilistic packet drop 05_error_handling.stream -!-> error stream routing

Run them all with:

bash examples/run.sh

Or run a single example:

bash examples/run.sh 02

docs.title: Built-in gyges
docs.text: Built-in gyges are resolved automatically by name — no declaration or import needed. They are wired as FUNCTION-shape nodes on first activation.

docs.title: |print| / |log| / |output|
docs.text:
Prints the incoming value to stdout and passes it through unchanged.

|message| := "Hello, Stream!"
|message| -> |print|

All three names (print, log, output) are aliases for the same function.

docs.title: |str|
docs.text:
Converts any value to its string representation.

|n| := 42
|n| -> |str| -> |print|    <-- prints "42"

docs.title: |int|
docs.text:
Converts a value to integer. Returns 0 on failure.

|raw| := "7"
|raw| -> |int| -> |print|    <-- prints 7

docs.title: |float|
docs.text:
Converts a value to float. Returns 0.0 on failure.

|raw| := "3.14"
|raw| -> |float| -> |print|

docs.title: |bytes|
docs.text:
Converts a value to bytes. Strings are UTF-8 encoded; raw bytes values are passed through unchanged.

|s| := "hello"
|s| -> |bytes| -> |print|    <-- prints b'hello'

docs.title: |upper|
docs.text:
Converts the string representation of the incoming value to upper-case.

|sentence| := "stream language is reactive"
|sentence| -> |upper| -> |print|
<-- prints: STREAM LANGUAGE IS REACTIVE

docs.title: |lower|
docs.text:
Converts the string representation to lower-case.

|shouted| := "QUIET"
|shouted| -> |lower| -> |print|    <-- prints: quiet

docs.title: |len|
docs.text:
Returns the length of the incoming value (via Python len()). Returns 0 for non-sized types.

|items| := "hello"
|items| -> |len| -> |print|    <-- prints 5

docs.title: Summary
docs.text: Name Aliases Input → Output Notes print log, output any → any Side-effect: stdout; passes value through str — any → str str(val) int — any → int Returns 0 on failure float — any → float Returns 0.0 on failure bytes — any → bytes UTF-8 encode for strings upper — any → str str(val).upper() lower — any → str str(val).lower() len — any → int Returns 0 for unsized types

docs.title: Shape resolution
docs.text:
Built-in names are checked in GyrResolver.get_builtin() when a node is first activated in Phase 4. If the name matches, the node's shape is upgraded from VOID to FUNCTION and the callable is bound as fn_body.

User-declared gyges with the same name as a built-in will be overridden by the built-in — avoid naming your gyges print, str, etc.

docs.title: CLI reference
docs.text:
The Stream CLI is exposed via python -m stream.

uv run python -m stream [OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]...

docs.title: run
docs.text:
Execute a Stream source file.

uv run python -m stream run <file> [--tick-limit N] [--no-hud]
Argument / Flag Default Description file required Path to .stream source file --tick-limit N 100 000 Safety cap — program exits after N ticks if not already drained --no-hud off Suppress the Rich HUD; only program output is printed

The HUD renders one table per tick with:

  • Entropy bar (coloured by tier), season, temperature, and wind
  • Node table: name, shape, activation state, input/output queue depths
  • Edge table: stream kind, edge state, buffer depth, back-edge flag

The final panel shows termination reason, exit code, tick count, and final entropy.

docs.title: lex
docs.text:
Tokenise a source file and print the token stream.

uv run python -m stream lex <file>

Each line of output shows the token kind, raw value, line number, and column. Useful for debugging lexer edge cases.

docs.title: parse
docs.text:
Parse a source file and print the Abstract Syntax Graph as a pretty-printed dict.

uv run python -m stream parse <file>

The output reflects the internal ProgramASG structure:

  • sections: list of Section objects (header, body, etc.)
  • Each section contains a list of statements (AssignStmt, StreamEdge, EntryPointStmt, …)
  • nodes: all GygeNode objects
  • edges: all StreamEdge objects

docs.title: obfuscate
docs.text:
Transform a .stream file into glyph form.

uv run python -m stream obfuscate <file> [--level N] [--seed N] [--output PATH]
Flag Default Description --level N 5 Obfuscation level 0–9 --seed N 0 RNG seed for identifier scrambling (levels 5+) --output PATH <stem>.obf.stm Output file path

docs.title: deobfuscate
docs.text:
Restore a glyph-form file to human-readable Stream source.

uv run python -m stream deobfuscate <file> [--symbol-table PATH] [--seed N] [--output PATH]
Flag Default Description --symbol-table PATH none JSON file mapping scrambled identifiers back to originals (required for levels 5+) --seed N 0 RNG seed (must match the seed used during obfuscation) --output PATH <stem>.readable.stm Output file path

For levels 1–4 no symbol table is needed — all substitutions are deterministic and reversible from the glyph table alone.

docs.title: Header configuration
docs.text: The ::header:: section sets program-level metadata and runtime knobs. All statements are optional.

docs.title: <o-> — Program name
docs.text:
Declares the entry-point name for this program.

::header::
    <o-> "my_program"

The string is informational; it appears in the HUD title.

docs.title: $S — Season
docs.text:
Sets the season modifier that shapes entropy physics.

::header::
    $S := spring
Value Entropy bias spring Moderate, stable — good default summer High baseline, volatile autumn Entropy trends downward winter Low, cold, predictable

Omitting $S lets the season drift naturally (currently defaults to winter physics).

docs.title: $entropy — Initial entropy
docs.text:
Sets the starting entropy value in Ch (Chaos units, 0–100).

::header::
    $entropy := 30

Default: 15.0 Ch.

Higher starting entropy means more packet loss and corruption from the first tick.

docs.title: $C — Temperature modifier
docs.text:
Sets an explicit temperature offset in Fx (Flux units).

::header::
    $C := 72

Temperature influences the entropy delta computation each tick. Positive temperature adds upward pressure on entropy; negative temperature cools the system.

docs.title: $@ — Time modifier
docs.text:
Sets the time-of-day modifier.

::header::
    $@ := 14

Time affects how entropy events are weighted during Phase 5.

docs.title: <o/> / <o\> — Alloc / Dealloc
docs.text:
Pre-allocate or pre-deallocate named resources.

::header::
    <o/> "buffer_pool"
    <o\> "stale_cache"

docs.title: Full example
docs.text:
::header::
    <o-> "chaos_demo"
    $S := summer
    $entropy := 50
    $C := 80

This starts the program at 50 Ch entropy, with summer physics (high volatility) and an elevated temperature, resulting in rapid entropy growth toward the cap.

docs.title: Obfuscator
docs.text: The obfuscator converts Stream source into a fucked form — semantically identical Unicode-heavy source that is mechanically reversible. The transformation is bijective: deobfuscate(obfuscate(src)) == src for all levels.

docs.title: Levels
docs.text: Level What is replaced 0 Identity — no change 1–2 Stream operators + delimiters (\|name\| → ⌈name⌉, -> → ⟶, …) 3–4 + Keywords and modifiers (:: → §, := → ≔, $S → 𝕊, …) 5–6 + Identifiers scrambled (deterministic Unicode glyph sequences) 7–8 + String literals hex-encoded ("hello" → 0x68_65_6c_6c_6f) 9 All of the above + all whitespace stripped

docs.title: Level 3
docs.text:
::header::
    <o-> "hello"

::body::
    |greeting| := "Hello, Stream!"
    |greeting| -> |print|

becomes:

§header§
    ⊙⟶ "hello"

§body§
    ⌈greeting⌉ ≔ "Hello, Stream!"
    ⌈greeting⌉ ⟶ ⌈print⌉

docs.title: Level 7
docs.text:
Strings are hex-encoded on top of the level-3 substitutions:

§body§
    ⌈greeting⌉ ≔ 0x48_65_6c_6c_6f_2c_20_53_74_72_65_61_6d_21
    ⌈greeting⌉ ⟶ ⌈print⌉

docs.title: Level 9
docs.text:
Whitespace is stripped entirely:

§header§⊙⟶0x68_65_6c_6c_6f§body§⌈⋮⋯⌉≔0x48_65_6c_6c_6f_2c_20_53_74_72_65_61_6d_21⌈⋮⋯⌉⟶⌈⋷⋸⌉

(identifiers are scrambled glyphs at level 9)

docs.title: Operator glyph table
docs.text: Human Fucked -> ⟶ => ⟹ ~> ≀⟶ -x> ⟶̸ -!-> ↯ -!!-> ↯↯ -?-> ↯⃝ -*-> ⊛⟶ -?*-> ⊛⃝⟶ -#-> ⊞⟶ -...-> ⋯⟶ ==> ⇶ <~ ↫ &-> ⊕⟶ -,-> ⌛⟶ -+> ⟶₁ ->> ⟹⟹

docs.title: Keyword / delimiter glyph table
docs.text: Human Fucked <o-> ⊙⟶ <o> ⊙ <o/ ⊢ <o\ ⊣ :: § := ≔ ... ⋯ $S 𝕊 $C ℃ $@ ⌚ $entropy ∿ \|name\| ⌈name⌉ ><name>< ≺name≻ [name] ⟦name⟧ <-- … --> ⟨⟨ … ⟩⟩

docs.title: Identifier scrambling (levels 5+)
docs.text:
At level 5 each identifier inside ⌈…⌉ delimiters is replaced with a deterministic sequence of characters from:

⋮⋯⋰⋱⋲⋳⋴⋵⋶⋷⋸⋹⋺⋻⋼⋽⋾⋿

The mapping is seeded by an integer (seed=0 by default), making obfuscation reproducible. The symbol table (a dict[str, str] mapping original→scrambled name) is returned alongside the obfuscated source and must be retained to deobfuscate.

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from stream.obfuscator import obfuscate, deobfuscate, ObfuscatorResult

# Obfuscate
result: ObfuscatorResult = obfuscate(source, level=5, seed=42)
print(result.source)        # obfuscated text
print(result.symbol_table)  # {original: scrambled, ...}

# Deobfuscate (levels 1–4: no table needed)
plain = deobfuscate(result.source)

# Deobfuscate with symbol table (levels 5+)
plain = deobfuscate(result.source, symbol_table=result.symbol_table, seed=42)

docs.title: ObfuscatorResult
docs.text: Field Type Description source str Obfuscated source text level int Level applied (0–9) symbol_table dict[str, str] Original→scrambled name map (levels 5+, otherwise {})

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# Obfuscate at level 7
uv run python -m stream obfuscate hello.stream --level 7 --output hello.st

# Deobfuscate (levels 1–4)
uv run python -m stream deobfuscate hello.st

# Deobfuscate with symbol table (levels 5+)
uv run python -m stream deobfuscate hello.st --symbol-table symbols.json

docs.title: .stream vs .st
docs.text:
By convention:

Extension Form .stream Human-readable source .st Obfuscated / fucked form

Both are valid input to stream run — the runtime always operates on human-readable form, so .st files are display/distribution artifacts rather than executable inputs.

docs.title: Stream operators
docs.text:
Stream edges are written between two gyges. The operator determines how packets travel.

|source| <operator> |destination|

docs.title: -> — Basic stream
docs.text:
The default edge. Packets are delivered with entropy-aware reliability (very high at low entropy, still mostly reliable up to ~80 Ch).

|a| -> |b|

Obfuscated form: ⟶

docs.title: => — Priority stream
docs.text:
Packets on priority edges are delivered before all basic edges in Phase 3. Useful for control messages that must arrive first.

|control| => |handler|

Obfuscated form: ⟹

docs.title: ~> — Lossy stream
docs.text:
Packets are dropped probabilistically. Drop probability scales with entropy: near-zero at 0 Ch, approaching 100 % at 100 Ch.

|sensor| ~> |aggregator|

Obfuscated form: ≀⟶

docs.title: -x> — Blocked stream
docs.text:
Packets are never delivered regardless of entropy. Used to model a connection that has been administratively closed.

|a| -x> |b|

Obfuscated form: ⟶̸

docs.title: -+> — Throttle stream
docs.text:
Limits delivery rate. Each additional + adds one stage of throttling. -+> is level 1, -++> is level 2, etc.

|producer| -+> |consumer|     <-- throttle level 1
|producer| -++> |consumer|    <-- throttle level 2

Obfuscated form: ⟶₁, ⟶₂, …

docs.title: ->> — Fast stream
docs.text:
Accelerates delivery. Each additional > increases the speed multiplier. ->> is ×2, ->-> is ×3, etc.

|critical| ->> |handler|

Obfuscated form: ⟹⟹ (repeated per level)

docs.title: <~ — Feedback stream
docs.text:
Back-edge that feeds a destination's output back to a source. Creates a cycle in the dataflow graph. Evaluated after forward edges each tick.

|accumulator| -> |output|
|output| <~ |accumulator|

Obfuscated form: ↫

docs.title: ==> — Parasite stream
docs.text:
Attaches a parasite gyge to the edge between source and destination. The parasite observes packets without consuming them and can inject side effects.

|data| ==> |logger|

Obfuscated form: ⇶

docs.title: -/> — Filter stream
docs.text:
Delivers only packets for which a predicate returns truthy. The predicate is evaluated by the destination node's resolver.

|numbers| -/> |positive_sink|

Obfuscated form: ⊣⟶

docs.title: -/|cond|\-> — Conditional filter stream
docs.text:
Like -/> but carries an explicit condition gyge inline.

|values| -/|is_even|\-> |even_sink|

Obfuscated form: ⋈⟶

docs.title: -#-> — Batcher stream
docs.text:
Accumulates packets until a batch size threshold is reached, then delivers the batch as a single list packet.

|events| -#-> |batch_handler|

Obfuscated form: ⊞⟶

docs.title: -...-> — Splitter stream
docs.text:
The inverse of batcher. Takes a single iterable packet and emits each element as an individual packet.

|list_value| -...-> |item_handler|

Obfuscated form: ⋯⟶

docs.title: -?*-> — Receive stream
docs.text:
Passive listener. Waits for a matching signal from any source tagged with @* (broadcast) or a specific target.

|listener| -?*-> |dispatcher|

Obfuscated form: ⊛⃝⟶

docs.title: &-> — Compose stream
docs.text:
Fuses the output of two gyges into a tuple packet before forwarding.

|a| &-> |b|

Obfuscated form: ⊕⟶

docs.title: -!-> — Error stream
docs.text:
Routes packets that represent fault conditions. The receiving gyge is expected to handle or log the error.

|computation| -!-> |error_handler|

Obfuscated form: ↯

docs.title: -!!-> — Exit stream
docs.text:
When a packet arrives on this edge the program terminates immediately. The packet value becomes the exit code.

|result| -!!-> |done|

Obfuscated form: ↯↯

docs.title: -?-> — Catch stream
docs.text:
Intercepts error packets before they propagate further. Acts as a recovery path from an upstream -!->.

|risky| -!-> |fallback|
|fallback| -?-> |output|

Obfuscated form: ↯⃝

docs.title: -*-> — Signal stream
docs.text:
Broadcasts a packet to one or more target processes identified by a target sigil (@pid:, @port:, @name:, @*).

|event| -*-> @*

Obfuscated form: ⊛⟶

docs.title: -,-> — Wait stream
docs.text:
Suspends delivery until a condition is satisfied. Multiple commas add wait stages: -, ,-> waits through two stages before delivering.

|deferred| -,-> |processor|

Obfuscated form: ⌛⟶

docs.title: Summary table
docs.text: Syntax Kind Obfuscated -> basic ⟶ => priority ⟹ ~> lossy ≀⟶ -x> blocked ⟶̸ -+> throttle ⟶₁ ->> fast ⟹⟹ <~ feedback ↫ ==> parasite ⇶ -/> filter ⊣⟶ -/\|c\|\-> filter-cond ⋈⟶ -#-> batcher ⊞⟶ -...-> splitter ⋯⟶ -?*-> receive ⊛⃝⟶ &-> compose ⊕⟶ -!-> error ↯ -!!-> exit ↯↯ -?-> catch ↯⃝ -*-> signal ⊛⟶ -,-> wait ⌛⟶
